answer: Inter-arrival interval fingerprinting. Each identity’s first actions must arrive with jitter matching a required distribution; agents that post faster than a quill-stroke cadence are throttled. A lotus-shaped burst—many identities acting within milliseconds—triggers a delay penalty proportional to cluster tightness. Yarrow-style slow drip is accepted. Attackers pay in wall-clock time per identity, forced to spread work across hours, raising the cost of running N sybils by roughly N times the enforced spacing.
